question: What is the main sign that a medical situation is a true life-threatening emergency?

options.A: Any illness that requires admission to a private room
options.B: Any injury that causes moderate joint and muscle pain
options.C: Immediate failure of one or more vital organ systems
options.D: A chronic condition that lasts longer than six months

explanation: Life-threatening emergencies mean vital organs are shutting down fast. Without quick help, this can lead to serious danger. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses look beyond the obvious symptoms when a patient's condition is crashing?

options.A: To ensure the hospital billing department receives correct insurance data
options.B: Because lab technicians require secondary confirmation for all tests
options.C: So that family members can be discharged home earlier in the shift
options.D: Because primary organ failure quickly triggers a cascade affecting other systems

explanation: When one major organ starts failing, it quickly pulls other vital systems down with it. Checking the whole patient keeps you steps ahead! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h1)

question: What makes blunt force trauma to the abdomen so dangerous?

options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does a tension pneumothorax cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure?

options.A: Trapped chest air compresses the heart and large blood vessels, reducing blood return
options.B: The patient stops breathing entirely due to complete paralysis of the diaphragm
options.C: Air travels directly into the bloodstream and dissolves all red blood cells
options.D: Fluid fills the lung tissue and drowns the patient from the inside out

explanation: Think of trapped air in the chest like a tight clamp pressing down on the heart and major blood vessels, stopping blood from flowing properly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main problem when the heart suddenly fails to pump properly?

options.A: An immediate and permanent increase in body temperature
options.B: Complete paralysis of the skeletal muscles in the lower limbs
options.C: Uncontrolled overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: A dangerous drop in systemic blood pressure and oxygen delivery

explanation: If the heart pump slows or stops, pressure drops and oxygen stops reaching the tissues that need it most. Spotting this early saves lives! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h3)

question: A patient arrives with a massive pulmonary embolism. What is happening in their body?

options.A: Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries is blocked, impairing oxygenation
options.B: The liver has stopped producing clotting factors, causing widespread bleeding
options.C: An infection in the urinary tract has spread into the spinal fluid
options.D: Gastric acid is leaking directly into the peritoneal cavity through an ulcer

explanation: A pulmonary embolism is a blocked blood vessel in the lungs. Because the blockage is there, blood can't pick up fresh oxygen to circulate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which part of the body suffers damage first when a person's airway is completely blocked?
explanation: The brain uses up oxygen extremely fast! That is why the airway is always our number one priority in any emergency. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why does a severe opioid overdose lead to dangerous breathing problems?

options.A: It causes immediate physical swelling and closure of the main vocal cords
options.B: It depresses the respiratory control center in the brainstem, reducing breathing rate
options.C: It freezes the movement of the diaphragm muscle by destroying motor nerves
options.D: It triggers severe allergic bronchospasm in the small bronchial airways

explanation: Opioids affect the part of the brain that tells the body to breathe, causing breathing to slow down and eventually stop if untreated. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is a major effect of severe heatstroke on the body's cells?

options.A: Disruption of vital enzymatic reactions and cellular function
options.B: Complete cessation of electrical activity in the skeletal muscles
options.C: Rapid production of large quantities of protective body fat
options.D: Permanent freezing of blood vessels in the upper extremities

explanation: Extreme heat scrambles the delicate proteins and enzymes our cells need to work. Cooling the patient down quickly is a true medical emergency priority! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal way that toxic substances cause a medical emergency?

options.A: Disrupting cellular oxygen use at the tissue level
options.B: Blocking the normal electrical signals of the heart
options.C: Stimulating the production of healthy bone marrow cells
options.D: Causing sudden and profound systemic vasodilation

explanation: Making healthy blood cells in the bone marrow is a good, normal process! Toxins cause harm by damaging systems, not by boosting healthy growth. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: When doing an emergency primary survey (ABCDE), what do you check first?
explanation: Always start with 'A' for Airway! Making sure air can move freely into the lungs comes before anything else. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h6)

question: An unresponsive patient is brought in. After you make sure their airway and breathing are okay, what is your next immediate step?

options.A: Inquiring about dietary preferences for hospital meals
options.B: Checking circulation, pulse rate, and blood pressure
options.C: Reviewing the patient's employment history and workplace
options.D: Measuring the exact height and weight on a scale

explanation: Following the ABCDE routine, 'C' comes right after Airway and Breathing so you can check for blood flow and signs of shock. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h6)
